units.introduced_year_basis: This tariff only evaluates a given two-dimensional vector and its magnitude; no vector calculus or vector constant-acceleration formula is needed.
units.difficulty_basis: Evaluate the two velocity components at the stated time and take their Euclidean magnitude.
units.summary: Find speed from a supplied velocity vector.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Apply power differentiation to each component of the supplied velocity vector.
units.summary: Differentiate a planar velocity to find acceleration.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Integrate both velocity components, determine their two constants from the supplied position at t=4 and evaluate the resulting vector at t=1.
units.summary: Integrate planar velocity to obtain a position.

exceptions: Visually verified v=3t²i−6t^(1/2)j; the extracted line breaks can misread the square-root power. The position condition before (c) is an interstitial printed given.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Resolve the known normal reaction to determine the horizontal force, then balance along the incline and use the signed result to identify friction’s direction.
units.summary: Find the magnitude and direction of static incline friction.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Recalculate the normal reaction after the horizontal force is removed, model kinetic friction and apply Newton’s second law down the slope.
units.summary: Find acceleration down a rough inclined plane after release.

exceptions: Inclined-plane geometry, horizontal force direction and tan(α)=3/4 visually verified. Part (b) requires a new reaction after the force is removed and does not reuse the earlier static friction.

units.introduced_year_basis: Adding two supplied force vectors and applying Newton’s second law in fixed component directions is AS scope; no general planar kinematic formula is needed.
units.difficulty_basis: Add the two coplanar force vectors and use proportional components of the resultant, parallel to the initial motion from rest, to establish the printed relation.
units.summary: Derive a force-parameter relation from a motion direction.

units.introduced_year_basis: The mark scheme explicitly allows taking the resultant-force magnitude followed by scalar s=ut+½at². The planar context does not require the additional A level vector suvat extension.
units.difficulty_basis: Use the parameter relation explicitly printed in (a), determine the resultant-force magnitude and apply scalar constant-acceleration displacement from rest along the fixed straight path.
units.summary: Find a fixed-direction travel distance under a resultant force.

exceptions: The source and mark scheme were checked: (a) prints λ−3μ+7=0, usable unscored in (b). The mark scheme for (b) explicitly provides scalar-distance alternatives as well as the vector route, supporting Year 12 classification.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Identify the leftward horizontal component of tension and use horizontal equilibrium to infer the opposing friction direction.
units.summary: Explain the direction of ground friction on a supported rod.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Take moments about the ground contact, place the uniform rod weight at its midpoint and include the attached particle’s lever arm.
units.summary: Find a rod’s string tension using moments.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Use the tension formula explicitly printed in (b), resolve its vertical component and balance it with both weights at the supplied angle.
units.summary: Find a rod’s vertical ground reaction.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Use the tension and reaction results explicitly printed in (b),(c), resolve the horizontal force and apply F=μR.

exceptions: Rod, perpendicular-string geometry, cos(θ)=3/5 and printed reaction 57Mg/25 visually verified. Later units retain the exact printed show-that formulas as unscored context; no unprinted answer is supplied.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Resolve the initial speed, form the horizontal range and zero-net-height equations and eliminate the flight time to establish the printed identity.
units.summary: Derive a projectile range identity from horizontal and vertical motion.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Use zero vertical speed at the maximum height, combine this with the range identity explicitly printed in (a) and eliminate the launch angle.
units.summary: Determine projectile launch speed from range and peak height.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Explain why a larger initial speed is needed to retain the same horizontal range in the refined resistive model.
units.summary: Compare launch speeds when air resistance is included.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Identify a physical refinement beyond the air resistance already included, such as ball size or spin.
units.summary: Suggest another refinement to a golf-ball projectile model.

exceptions: The source range 120 m, maximum height 10 m and printed identity U²sin(α)cos(α)=588 were visually checked. The identity is retained unscored for (b); the later qualitative units do not need the numerical launch-speed answer.
